# Unified CLI Command Reference

The only public application launcher is `synesis`.

The commands below are generated from the CLI's own command tree (`CommandReferenceTest` fails when this list drifts); each description is the first sentence of what `synesis <command> --help` prints.

Ordinary project commands discover `.synesis` from the current directory. An
advanced `--profile <dir>` override is available on commands that support
isolated process tests and cross-profile experiments. Hook JSON stays on
stdout; diagnostics stay on stderr and hook exit code remains 0 for provider
contract responses.

`synesis --version` and `synesis version` report the same embedded build
version. Lifecycle workflows accept one operation mode per invocation;
combining dry-run, prepare, inspect, execute, or rollback modes is a usage
error. `workspace mutate` requires the exact `--session`; `--create-only` and
`--previous-hash` are exclusive preconditions checked under the assigned
worktree's cross-process mutation lock. An idempotency key replays only the
same project, provider binding, target, mutation kind, content, preconditions,
and output mode; reusing it with changed input is rejected.

Provider installation commands are project-local. Provider commands use
canonical IDs only. Codex MCP project context comes from the connected workspace
or process working directory; `synesis mcp --project` is not supported. Managed
Codex launches carry their pinned project root through trusted server
configuration. The global MCP registration is removed only with
`synesis provider uninstall codex --global`.

A `synesis provider` command that cannot find its project says why on standard
error: `ERROR=PROJECT_NOT_CONFIGURED` for a directory that is not an initialized
project, otherwise the cause (`ERROR=PROJECT_INVALID`, `ERROR=MALFORMED`,
`ERROR=PROJECT_ACCESS_FAILED`) with a `REASON=` line. Exit code 10 as before. Each
refusal also prints `MESSAGE=` and `FIX=` (see "Errors and exit codes").

`synesis mcp` also asks the installation daemon for the runtime of a project
shared with another computer, in the background and only when it is not
running, so an interactive agent's session after a reboot replicates and
transfers code like one started by `agents run`. It prints nothing to standard
output, which is the protocol's; a failure goes to standard error as
`SYNESIS_MCP_RUNTIME=UNAVAILABLE`. A project on one computer is left alone.

`synesis agents run` starts one headless session per `--agent`, gives each the
same prompt on standard input, and waits. A headless agent ends its process when
it has nothing left to do in one turn, including when it has polled its inbox
unchanged as often as the protocol allows. When such an agent has stopped, a
lane of its provider is still open, and other work has progressed since, the
command starts that agent's own provider session again with one sentence telling
it to continue. A provider writes its closing message after its last call, and
an agent that has decided to stop may still call once more, so an agent is taken
to have acted on the project only up to the earlier of its last recorded call
and 30 seconds before its process ended: work recorded after that also resumes
it, at the cost of one extra turn when the agent had in fact seen it. The command reads only the durable coordination log: it never reads or
relays an agent's conversation, never assigns work or picks a continuation, and
never writes to the coordination log. Heartbeats and lane takeovers do not count
as progress, so two idle agents cannot wake each other. A resumed agent is a new
connection and therefore a new session; it regains its lane through the ordinary
recovery and continuation path.

The command never invents a task. At a terminal (standard input and output are
a terminal, and neither `--porcelain` nor `SYNESIS_OUTPUT=porcelain` was given),
with neither `--prompt` nor `--prompt-file`, it asks once, "What should the agents
work on?", after it has checked the project, the providers and the options, prints
the answer back as `AGENT_TASK=`, and starts only on a non-empty answer. In a
script, with a blank task, or with an empty answer it prints
`ERROR=TASK_REQUIRED`, `MESSAGE=agents run needs a task` and `FIX=pass --prompt
"<task>" or --prompt-file <file>`, exits 2 and starts no agent. (Until
2026-10-20 the `ERROR=` line carried that sentence instead of the code; the
sentence is now the `MESSAGE=`. The other usage refusals of `agents run` follow
the same rule: `ERROR=` is the code, `MESSAGE=` the sentence.)

Before it starts any agent, the command asks the installation daemon for the
project's runtime, starting both when they are not running, and prints
`PROJECT_RUNTIME=READY`. When they cannot be started, a project shared with
another computer is refused with `ERROR=PROJECT_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE`, because
its agents reach that computer only through the runtime; a project on one
computer prints `PROJECT_RUNTIME=UNAVAILABLE` and starts the agents.

That path starts when a connection is known to have ended. A provider that kills
its MCP server instead of closing it leaves no such proof, and Synesis would
otherwise wait out its five-minute abrupt-loss grace period. The command gives
each process it starts its own connection identity and, when the process exits,
records that connection as closed in the project's session leases. It can do
this only for processes it started.

A lane bound to another lane's contract that owes an action counts as absent
after a stated time without a verified call (two minutes by default;
`SYNESIS_REQUESTER_ANSWER_GRACE_SECONDS` or the system property
`synesis.requesterAnswerGraceSeconds` changes it). The log does not change when
that time passes, so the command also resumes a stopped owner once when such a
deadline of its provider has passed, and does not end the run while one is
still pending. The owner's next read is what raises the operator request.

Work can also move without any agent of this run. When every agent has stopped
and nothing progressed, the command keeps waiting while a participant it did not
start (another computer's agent, an interactive agent) holds an open lane, or
while another computer of the project is connected (for the leader a member, for
a member its leader, as `replication.log` last recorded) and an agent here can
come back to an open lane of its own: that computer's agents can still claim the
review or give the admission the lane waits for. Their progress resumes the
agents here as above. Each wait lasts at most until `--timeout-minutes`, and its
start is printed once as `AGENT_RUN_WAITING=FOREIGN_LANE_OPEN`,
`AGENT_RUN_WAITING=OTHER_COMPUTER_CONNECTED` or, for the answer period above,
`AGENT_RUN_WAITING=ANSWER_DEADLINE`.

The command ends with `AGENT_RUN_RESULT`: `COMPLETED` when no lane is open and
every work group that ever had a lane is closed (a group created ahead of its
lanes that never received one holds no work) and at least one group finished its work,
`ALL_WORK_CANCELLED` when nothing is open because every lane was cancelled, `NEEDS_OPERATOR` when every agent has stopped
and an operator request is open (each is printed as `OPERATOR_REQUEST=<id> CONDITION=<condition>`), `STALLED` when every agent
has stopped and nothing has progressed since, `NO_WORK_ANNOUNCED`, `RESUME_LIMIT_REACHED`, or
`TIMED_OUT`. Only `COMPLETED` exits with 0. Each provider must already be
installed in the project. Claude Code is limited to the Synesis tools and its read-only
tools. Codex is started in its read-only sandbox with the Synesis server's
tools approved (`sandbox_mode=read-only`,
`mcp_servers.synesis.default_tools_approval_mode=approve`), whatever the
user's Codex configuration says: a headless Codex session does not run the
project's hooks, so without this nothing kept its own file tool or a shell
command out of the project checkout (ADR-0091). Neither provider's policy is
ever loosened outside the Synesis tools. Agent output is kept as log files under the Synesis state directory,
outside the project.

`synesis coordination status` reads durable coordination state and changes
nothing. On a project shared across computers (ADR-0098) it adds
`REPLICATION_ROLE=leader|member`. A member also prints `REPLICATION_LEADER=<node>`
and `REPLICATION_STATE=CONNECTED|DISCONNECTED|DIVERGED|NO_COORDINATION_SERVER`. A
leader prints one `REPLICATION_MEMBER=<node> STATE=<state> since=<time>` line per
member its role file names, sorted by node: `STATE=CONNECTED` while that member's
session is attached, `STATE=DISCONNECTED` after it ended or, for a member that has
not connected since the leader's coordination server started, since that start
(with no `since` for a member added while that server runs that has not connected
yet), and `STATE=NO_COORDINATION_SERVER` with no `since` when that server is not
running. Both roles print `REPLICATION_LAST_DISCONNECT=<reason> <time> <details>`
for the last session that ended, when there is one. Further `KEY=VALUE` fields may
be added to these lines.

## Log dump

`synesis log dump [--project <dir>] [--type <TYPE>]` prints every coordination log
this computer holds, its own and each copy of another computer's, in the order this
computer applied the entries (ADR-0102 item 2). It only reads files: it works while
the project's runtime is stopped, takes no lock, and creates, moves or removes
nothing. Like every command, `--porcelain` (or output that is not a terminal) gives
the stable `KEY=VALUE` lines below.

- `LOG_DUMP=PASS`, `PROJECT_ID=<id>`, `LOG_ENTRIES=<n>` (the count after `--type`).
- One `LOG_ENTRY=pos=<n> log=<self|node> writer=<node> seq=<n> type=<TYPE> [<note>]
  [<field>=<value> ...]` line per entry. `pos` is the local revision, the entry's
  position among the entries that took effect here, or `-` when it has none. `log` is
  `self` for this computer's own log and the writer's node for a copy; `seq` is the
  position in that log. A `<note>` says why `pos` is `-`:
  `COUNTED_FOR_NOTHING code=<CODE>` (the entry arrived and a rule made it count for
  nothing) or `NOT_APPLIED` (a copy's entry with no line in `applied.order` yet). The
  fields name what the entry is about (`lane`, `group`, `task`, `snapshot`, `grant`,
  `verdict`, `combine`, `remerge`, `attempt`, `request`, `member`, `policy`,
  `revision`, ...); only the identifiers, refs and verdicts named for that type are
  printed. Keys, invitations and message text are never printed. A type this build
  does not know prints as `... seq=<n> UNKNOWN type=<wire code>`; an entry that cannot
  be read prints `type=UNREADABLE`.
- `LOG_PROBLEM=<log> <seq> <CODE>` for each thing that could not be read or does not
  hold (`ENTRY_MALFORMED`, `SIGNATURE_INVALID`, `CHAIN_BROKEN`, `WRONG_SIGNER`,
  `SEQUENCE_MISMATCH`, `OTHER_PROJECT`, `FILE_NAME_INVALID`, `FILE_UNREADABLE`) or,
  as `applied.order <line> LINE_MALFORMED`, a line of the applied order that cannot be
  parsed. The dump goes on after a problem.
- The summary, from the same projections a running computer replays: `SUMMARY_LANES=<n>`
  and one `SUMMARY_LANE=<id> state=ACTIVE|ENDED|UNKNOWN ...` per lane the logs name;
  `SUMMARY_GROUPS` / `SUMMARY_GROUP`; `SUMMARY_SNAPSHOTS` / `SUMMARY_SNAPSHOT` (state,
  `verdicts=<reviewer>:<verdict>,...`, `disputed=true`); `SUMMARY_GRANTS` /
  `SUMMARY_GRANT` (state `AVAILABLE|CONSUMED|REVOKED|SUPERSEDED|UNRESOLVED`) and
  `SUMMARY_REVIEW`; `SUMMARY_COMBINES` / `SUMMARY_COMBINE`; `SUMMARY_MEMBERSHIP` and
  `SUMMARY_JOIN_REQUEST`. When the logs cannot be replayed (a corrupt or unknown
  entry), the summary is the single line `SUMMARY_UNAVAILABLE=<reason>`.

`--type` keeps only entries of that type (any case; `UNKNOWN` matches unknown types)
and does not change the summary. The command is additive: further fields, notes,
problem codes and `SUMMARY_*` lines may be added.

## Project validation

A project can declare one command that must pass before its work is integrated.
It is project policy, kept as `validation` in `.synesis/project.json`, and it is
set here by whoever has authority over the project, never by an agent.

- `synesis project validation set [--timeout <seconds>] [--directory <dir>] [--also-in-lane] -- <argv>...`
  declares the command, replacing any the project declared. Everything after
  `--` is the executable and its arguments; no shell is used. `--timeout`
  defaults to 120 seconds and may be at most 3600. `--directory` is relative to
  the project root and defaults to `.`.
- `synesis project validation show` prints the declared command.
- `synesis project validation clear` removes it.

Each prints `VALIDATION=DECLARED` with `VALIDATION_ARGV` (a JSON array),
`VALIDATION_DIRECTORY`, `VALIDATION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS` and
`VALIDATION_ALSO_IN_LANE`, or `VALIDATION=NONE`. `set` and `clear` rewrite the
project file, keep its identity and review policy, and print
`PROJECT_FILE_CHANGED=.synesis/project.json`. When the project already declares
what was asked they change nothing and do not print that line.

Where Git tracks the project file, `set` and `clear` also commit it, that one
file alone, and print `PROJECT_FILE_COMMITTED=<short commit>`: nothing is
integrated into a checkout that holds an uncommitted change. They are refused
with `ERROR=CONTROL_CHECKOUT_FOREIGN_CHANGES` when the checkout already holds
changes Synesis did not make, by the rule integration itself uses, so the
untracked files a provider installs (`.claude/`, `.codex/`, `.mcp.json`) do
not count; an untracked `AGENTS.md` is the user's and does count (ADR-0103 decision 9). When the commit fails, the file is put back as it
was and the command reports `ERROR=PROJECT_COMMIT_FAILED`. Outside a Git
repository, or where Git does not track the file, the file is rewritten and
nothing is committed. Both commands wait for an integration attempt that is
running, for at most two seconds, and are refused when it runs longer: run them
again when it has ended.

The command runs on the combined work: the snapshots of an integration attempt
applied to the project's head in a separate worktree, before the project's
branch moves. With `--also-in-lane` it also runs in each lane alone before that
lane's finish is published. That is off by default, because a lane whose tests
need another lane's code cannot pass the command alone.

When the command exits non-zero on the combined work, the snapshot added last
to the attempt is refused. Its lane is reopened and shown what the command
printed, corrects its own files and publishes again; the other snapshots are
tried without it. A lane is asked to repair twice. When the command fails while
a lane with a snapshot in the attempt has used its two repairs, when it timed
out or could not be started, or when the pass that ran it died twice in a row,
nothing is refused and Synesis raises an operator request with condition
`integration_validation_failing`. The command runs while the project's event
log is locked, so other writers wait or are refused for as long as it runs.

## Operator requests

When only someone with authority over the project can clear what blocks it,
Synesis records an operator request (ADR-0091). It raises one for a project
checkout holding changes Synesis did not make (nothing is integrated into such
a checkout, and the work that is finished waits), and for a lane bound to
another lane's contract that owes an action while its agent has not returned
(ADR-0092): start the agents again so one continues that lane. It raises one
with condition `integration_validation_failing` when the project's validation
command fails on the work waiting to be integrated and no lane is asked to
repair it. Nothing is integrated while that request is open and the command is
not run again by the agents' own calls. Change the command, change the project
or end the lane, then run `synesis operator recheck`: it is the one pass that
runs the command again. The request closes when the command then passes or
refuses a snapshot, when the project declares no command, or when no snapshot
is waiting; after a lane is ended, the pass that blocks its snapshot is
followed by the pass that closes the request. A recheck that fails in another
way, or prints something else, closes the request and raises a new one, so the
open request always shows the latest output.

`synesis operator list` prints the open requests, each with a `SUMMARY` and its
`EVIDENCE` lines exactly as the refusing tool reported them (`--all` adds the
closed ones). `synesis operator recheck` looks again and integrates what was
waiting; it exits with 0 when no request is left open. No command declares a
request Synesis raised resolved: it closes when its condition is observed not
to hold.

An agent can also put something to the operator itself (ADR-0093). Such a
request is listed with `CONDITION=lane_asks_operator` and `RAISED_BY_LANE`, blocks
nothing, and makes a run that stalls end `NEEDS_OPERATOR`. Synesis cannot observe
that it was dealt with, so `synesis operator close <id> [--because <text>]`
closes it.

## Trash

Work that leaves an agent's hands is kept, never deleted on its own (ADR-0098
step 7): the worktree of a lane another computer took over while this one was
away (`TAKEN_OVER`), a snapshot finished after its work group's goal was met
(`LATE_FOR_MET_GOAL`), and a snapshot still disputed or rejected when its work
group completed (`DISPUTE_GIVEN_UP`). Each is a commit under
`refs/synesis/trash/<lane>/<epoch>` on the computer that trashed it, which any
computer of the project can fetch.

`synesis trash list` prints one `TRASH=<lane> EPOCH=<epoch> REASON=...` line per
piece of work. `synesis trash restore <lane> <epoch>` brings it back in a work
group of its own, with the original's review policy; a lane announced in that
group starts with the work in its worktree. `synesis trash empty <lane> <epoch>
--yes` deletes it for good, on every computer: the one deletion of work Synesis
makes, and it cannot be undone.

## Conversations

`synesis conversations` lists what agents said to each other, one line per
conversation with its members and message count; `synesis conversations <id>`
prints that conversation's messages. It only reads: the operator cannot post.

## Errors and exit codes

A setup refusal of `synesis provider`, `synesis link` and `synesis agents run`
prints three keys, in this order, in human and `--porcelain` output alike:

```text
ERROR=<CODE>     stable; listed below
MESSAGE=<what happened, one sentence>
FIX=<one command or step that resolves it>
```

They are added beside what each command printed before: `REASON=`, `HINT=`, the
`PROVIDER_*_RESULT=` line, `LINK_STATE=` and `LINK_FAILURE=` stay as they were
and are removed only in a separately authorized change. The shape goes where the
command already printed its `ERROR=` (standard error for `link` and `agents run`
and for a project that cannot be found; standard output for a provider result,
which carries its own `ERROR=`). A code that is not listed still gets a
`MESSAGE=` and a `FIX=`. `synesis doctor` failing to run prints the same
three after its prose line.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `0` | The command did what was asked. |
| `1` | A valid command could not finish its operation: an invitation that ended without a connection or ran out of `--wait-seconds`, an agent run that did not complete, a degraded provider status. |
| `2` | Invalid usage: a syntax error, conflicting options, an unknown provider, a missing task. |
| `3` | Today only `synesis provider status` returns it, for a broken integration. It is reserved for `synesis doctor --strict`, as its name says. |
| `10` | Local identity, project or configuration failure: the project cannot be found or read, the runtime cannot be reached, a provider file cannot be written. |
| `11` | The invitation is not valid (`INVITE_INVALID`). |
| `12` | The host's identity did not match the invitation. |
| `13` | The network session failed. |
| `14` | The answer link is not valid, was used, or expired (`ANSWER_INVALID`). |
| `15` | The other computer runs a Synesis with another link compatibility number (`INCOMPATIBLE_VERSION`). |
| `70` | An unexpected failure, reported without its details. |

`synesis doctor --strict` still returns `10` when the project is not healthy.
Moving it to `3`, and provider results off `2` and `3`, is a separate change that
needs the owner's approval (ADR-0103, decision 6).

### Codes of the project lookup

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `PROJECT_NOT_CONFIGURED` | The folder is not an initialized project. |
| `NOT_FOUND` | The same, as `synesis link` has always reported it. |
| `PROJECT_INVALID` | `--project` names a folder that cannot be used. |
| `MALFORMED` | The project's metadata file is damaged. |
| `PROJECT_ACCESS_FAILED` | Anything else went wrong reading the project; `REASON=` says what. |
| `METADATA_ROOT_UNAVAILABLE` | Synesis's private storage for the project is unavailable or unsafe. |
| `GIT_HEAD_UNAVAILABLE` | The repository has no commit to build on. |
| `CONFLICT` | The project is partly set up or contradicts itself. |
| `PROJECT_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` | The project's runtime is not running and could not be started. |
| `INTERRUPTED` | The command was interrupted. |
| `DOCTOR_FAILED` | `synesis doctor` could not run. |

### Codes of `synesis provider`

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `UNKNOWN_PROVIDER` | No provider has that name. |
| `PROFILE_MISSING` | The project's profile folder is missing. |
| `LAUNCHER_MISSING` | The Synesis launcher the provider's hooks run was not found. |
| `MANUAL_INSTALL_FAILED` | The Synesis skill could not be written into the provider's user folder (`MANUAL_REASON=`). |
| `OBSOLETE_PROVIDER_STATE` | The provider's saved state comes from a Synesis that cannot be read. |
| `INVALID_CONFIG` | The provider's configuration file cannot be read. |
| `PROVIDER_CONFIGURATION_CONFLICT` | The configuration holds a Synesis entry Synesis did not write. |
| `INSTALL_FAILED` | The integration could not be installed. |
| `UNINSTALL_FAILED` | The integration could not be removed. |
| `GLOBAL_MCP_UNSUPPORTED` | The provider has no shared user-level MCP entry. |
| `GLOBAL_MCP_UNINSTALL_FAILED` | The shared user-level entry could not be removed. |
| `CONFLICTING_UNINSTALL_SCOPE` | `--global` and `--project` together. |
| `BROKEN` | The status check found the integration broken. |
| `PROVIDER_BROKEN` | A broken status without a cause of its own. |
| `PROVIDER_DEGRADED` | A degraded status without a cause of its own. |
| `MCP_CATALOG_MISMATCH` | The provider was installed by a Synesis whose tools differ. |
| `MANAGED_GUIDANCE_STALE` | The skill the provider reads is older than this Synesis. |
| `CONFLICTING_MODES` | More than one of `--dry-run`, `--prepare`, `--show-plan` and `--execute`. |
| `PROVIDER_MIGRATION_REVIEW_REQUIRED` | The provider configuration could not be migrated safely. |
| `PROVIDER_MIGRATION_STALE` | The prepared plan no longer matches the files. |

### Codes of `synesis link`

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `INVITE_INVALID` | The invitation is not valid, was changed, or expired. |
| `ANSWER_INVALID` | The answer link is not valid, was used, or expired. |
| `INCOMPATIBLE_VERSION` | The other computer's Synesis cannot talk to this one. |
| `INVALID_NODE_ID` | The text is not a node ID. |
| `PROJECT_FOLDER_NOT_EMPTY` | `--into` names a folder that holds files. |
| `PROJECT_NOT_ON_THIS_COMPUTER` | This computer does not have the invited project; join again with `--into`. |
| `PROJECT_FOLDER_INVALID` | The folder cannot be used for this invitation. |
| `PROJECT_FOLDER_NOT_THE_PROJECT` | The folder holds another project. |
| `PROJECT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` | The folder is not the project the invitation names. |
| `INVITER_IS_THIS_COMPUTER` | This computer made the invitation. |
| `FOLLOWING_ANOTHER_LEADER` | The project already follows another computer. |
| `ALREADY_A_LEADER` | The project already is the leader. |
| `LOG_NOT_EMPTY` | The project has its own history, so it cannot follow another's. |
| `OPERATION_NOT_FOUND` | The runtime no longer knows the invitation. |
| `JOIN_REQUEST_UNKNOWN` | No computer with that node ID is waiting. |
| `OPERATION_LIMIT` | Too many invitations are waiting. |
| `NO_USABLE_CANDIDATE` | No network route to the other computer was found. |
| `HOST_TIMEOUT` | The other computer did not answer in time. |
| `CONNECTION_FAILED` | The connection failed. |
| `EXPIRED` | The invitation expired unopened. |
| `DECLINED` | The other computer declined. |
| `CANCELLED` | The invitation was cancelled. |
| `SESSION_ENDED` | The other computer connected and the session ended at once. |
| `OPERATION_UNKNOWN` | The runtime forgot the invitation, for example after a restart. |
| `LINK_FAILED` | The invitation ended without a connection for a reason not listed; `LINK_FAILURE=` and `LINK_FAILURE_DETAIL=` say why. |
| `LINK_WAIT_TIMEOUT` | Nobody opened the invitation before `--wait-seconds` ran out. |
| `RUNTIME_REQUEST_REJECTED` | The runtime refused for a reason it did not name. |

### Codes of `synesis agents run`

| Code | When |
| --- | --- |
| `TASK_REQUIRED` | No task, a blank one, or an empty answer to the question. |
| `PROMPT_CONFLICT` | `--prompt` and `--prompt-file` together. |
| `AGENT_INVALID` | An `--agent` that is not `provider[:model[:effort]]`. |
| `PROVIDER_NOT_INSTALLED` | The provider is not installed in this project. |
| `AGENT_RUN_INVALID` | Another option is not valid. |
| `AGENT_RUN_INTERRUPTED` | The run was interrupted. |
| `AGENT_RUN_FAILED` | The run failed before it finished; `REASON=` says why. |
| `PROJECT_RUNTIME_UNAVAILABLE` | A shared project's runtime cannot be started, so no agent was started. |

## Doctor

`synesis doctor` keeps its summary lines and adds one section for each of three
groups. Each finding is marked `confirmed` (exact evidence), `suspected`
(strong but not exact, or contradictory evidence) or `advice` (worth knowing,
changes no health status) and carries a `FIX=`. Keys are `<GROUP>_STATUS`
(`OK`, `ATTENTION`, or `NOT_APPLICABLE` for the network group of a project that is
not shared), `<GROUP>_FINDINGS=<n>` and, for each finding,
`<GROUP>_FINDING_<n>=<code>` with `_MARK`, `_MESSAGE`, `_FIX` and the finding's
details. The groups are `ENVIRONMENT`, `NETWORK` and `WORK_GROUPS`; the summary
lines above them are unchanged and `--json` gains `groups` and, on every
finding, `group`, `mark` and `fix`.

| Group | Finding | Mark | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| environment | `git_missing` | confirmed | `git --version` does not run. |
| environment | `agent_not_on_path` | suspected | A connected agent's executable is not on this terminal's `PATH`. |
| environment | `provider_files_stale` | confirmed | A connected agent's hook, launcher, profile or skill is missing or does not match this Synesis. |
| environment | `installed_launcher_missing`, `provider_migration_required`, `provider_config_malformed`, `provider_config_synesis_entry_duplicated` | as before | Findings that existed before the groups. |
| network | `project_runtime_not_running` | suspected | A shared project whose runtime the installation daemon does not hold. |
| network | `link_firewall_missing`, `link_firewall_stale` | confirmed | Windows only: no rule, or a rule naming another version's `java.exe`. |
| work groups | `operator_requests_open` | advice | One or more operator requests wait for a person. |
| work groups | `stale_session_lease`, `ambiguous_session_liveness`, `cleanup_recommended` | as before | Findings that existed before the groups. |

`synesis doctor --fix` makes exactly three repairs and then reports again, with
`FIXES_APPLIED=`, one `FIX_APPLIED=` for each, `FIXES_SKIPPED=` and one
`FIX_SKIPPED=<code> REASON=...` for each repair that was due and could not be
made, and `MUTATIONS_PERFORMED=<number of repairs that changed something>`:

1. Synesis's own administrative state: stale lock files whose owning process is
   gone and corrupt plan files, which are archived, through the existing repair
   plan (`synesis repair`). `FIX_APPLIED=administrative_state COMPLETED=<n>`.
2. A connected agent whose managed files are out of date, written again like
   `synesis provider install <provider>`. `FIX_APPLIED=provider_files_stale PROVIDER=<id>`.
3. The runtime of a shared project, started like `synesis agents run` and the link
   commands start it. `FIX_APPLIED=project_runtime_not_running`.

It never changes anything a person wrote, the firewall rule, or an operator
request; those findings keep their `FIX=` for a person to run. With `--json` the
`FIX*` lines go to standard error, so standard output stays one JSON document.
`--strict` using exit code `3` is a later change.
